claim.pdf_says: Page 1023 (printed 993) ends with "Khmer:\n17B4-17D3, 17DD, 17E0-17E9". "Khojki:" is the FIRST line printed on page 1024 (printed 994), directly above "1122C-11237, 1123E".
claim.markdown_says: End of the page-1023 block: "Khmer:\n17B4-17D3, 17DD, 17E0-17E9 Khojki:". The page-1024 block then opens with a headless "1122C-11237, 1123E".
claim.why_it_matters: The script name Khojki is detached from its range 1122C-11237, 1123E in the normative Annex B table and appended to the Khmer entry.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED on both sides by direct inspection at 300 dpi; the claim quotes both sources verbatim. PDF page 1023 (printed folio 993): the last content line of the body is the Khmer entry, printed on two lines as 'Khmer:' / '17B4-17D3, 17DD, 17E0-17E9', followed by white space and then the footer '(C)ISO/IEC 2023 993'. There is no 'Khojki:' anywhere on page 1023 - I checked the full column down to the footer and the licence line. PDF page 1024 (printed folio 994): the running head 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' is followed by the first body line 'Khojki:', with '1122C-11237, 1123E' directly beneath it, then 'Khudawadi:' / '112DF-112EA, 112F0-112F9'. So in the PDF the label and its range sit together as a normal two-line entry that merely happens to start a page. Markdown (specs/ISO_COBOL.md): line 40875 'Khmer:', line 40876 '17B4-17D3, 17DD, 17E0-17E9 Khojki:', line 40877 blank, line 40878 the anchor, and line 40882 the headless '1122C-11237, 1123E'. The transcription therefore pulled the page-1024 label 'Khojki:' backward across the page boundary and concatenated it onto the page-1023 Khmer data line, leaving the Khojki range with no label. This is not reflow, wrapping, hyphenation, or page-break furniture: a script-name key from one table row has been merged into the value cell of the preceding row, so a structured read of this Annex B script/range table either loses '1122C-11237, 1123E' entirely or mis-attributes it, and 'Khojki' reads as part of the Khmer entry. Meaning is changed for any mechanical consumer, so real=true. Corroborating pattern (not part of this claim): the identical defect occurs at the 1022->1023 boundary - line 40824 reads '0AFA-0AFF Gunjala_Gondi:' and the page-1023 block then opens headless at line 40828 with '11D8A-11D8E, 11D90-11D91, 11D93-11D97, 11DA0-11DA9', while the PDF prints 'Gunjala_Gondi:' as the first body line of page 1023 above that range. The trailing-label-across-the-page-break bug is systematic through this table and should be swept, not fixed one boundary at a time.
verdict.corrected_description: The claim is accurate as written; no correction needed. Precise anchors for the fix: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 40876 must become '17B4-17D3, 17DD, 17E0-17E9' and 'Khojki:' must be reinserted as the first content line of the page-1024 block, immediately above line 40882 '1122C-11237, 1123E'. Scope note: this is one instance of a systematic page-boundary defect in the Annex B script/range table - the same trailing-label migration occurs at the 1022->1023 boundary (line 40824 '0AFA-0AFF Gunjala_Gondi:' leaving page 1023 headless), so the repair should be a sweep of every page break in this table rather than a single-line edit.
